chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ibn Muskān from al-Ḥalabī said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Zakat al-Fitr, and he said: 'Upon every person whom the man supports, whether free or slave, young or old, [is due] a sa' of dates or half a sa' of wheat, and the sa' is four amdad.'

key_terms.أَمْدَادٌ: Amdad (plural of midd, a smaller unit of volume)
key_terms.صَاعٌ: Sa' (a traditional unit of volume measurement)
key_terms.صَدَقَةِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr (alms of breaking the fast)

ai.seo_question: What is the exact amount and type of food required for Zakat al-Fitr according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the obligation of Zakat al-Fitr extends to all dependents—free or enslaved, adult or child—supported by the head of the household. It specifies the measure as one sa' of dates or half a sa' of wheat, defining the sa' as four amdad, reflecting the practical economic realities of the early Shia community. This detailed quantification underscores the juristic emphasis on ensuring the poor receive sufficient sustenance to celebrate Eid independently.
